why: A package tour operator with $1.3 billion bookings, supplier costs of 89% and running costs of 12% making a 1% loss is consistent and believable.
Both storage firms' cost shares and margins sum to 100%, and about 370 to 390 units per site with roughly 82% to 83% occupancy is believable.
Passenger-route profits of $8 to $24 million across 9 to 14 routes (about $0.6 to $2.7 million per route) are believable for ferry operators.
Loss probabilities of 20% to 50% and damages of $3 to $12 million per claim are believable for a software company's customer lawsuits.
Library incomes of $2 to $47 million (about $179 million in all) against 4 to 72 designers per library are believable for a loss-making e-learning firm.

With 5 small, 8 mid and 3 large-market clubs the group figures give a 50% average win rate and reproduce the stated $24 million revenue and $1.1 million profit, and the magnitudes are believable for a hockey league.
Late-handover probabilities of 10% to 40% and penalties of $3 to $16 million are believable for large construction projects.
Business-line revenues of $31 to $142 million with margins from 3% on hardware resale to about 35% on software licences are believable for an IT reseller.
The eight uses sum exactly to the 7.3 billion litres a week total (about 1,000 megalitres a day), believable for a regional water company with about 20% leakage.
A brewery sales manager on salary plus 3% of account orders and 15% of new-account first-year orders, working 7.5 hours a day, 5 days a week, 45 weeks a year, is believable.
